title: Short Stuff: Handwashing vs Dishwashers
summary: Short Stuff episode comparing handwashing and dishwashers. Hosts open with a reference to Judge John Hodgman's dishwashing-dispute cases, then argue that dishwashers, especially Energy Star models (under about four gallons per cycle), use less water than handwashing, which runs water continuously. They discuss hot water heater energy costs, the hygiene hypothesis, and a claim from Noah Horowitz of the Natural Resources Defense Council against pre-rinsing. They cover loading habits, scraping vs. pre-rinsing, upgrading old machines, and low-water handwashing with a two-tub sink. The episode ends with listener-style banter and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter on dishwashing disputes
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the topic, mentioning Judge John Hodgman's dishwashing-dispute cases and common marriage arguments about how to load a dishwasher. They joke about knives and silverware orientation.

segments.title: Misconception that handwashing saves energy
segments.summary: The hosts say they long believed handwashing used less energy and water and that a hygiene-hypothesis argument supported handwashing. They note a Cascade commercial prompted the research, which found the opposite.

segments.title: Dishwasher water use vs handwashing
segments.summary: Modern Energy Star dishwashers use under four gallons of water per cycle, while a handwashing faucet runs about 1.5 gallons per minute, so even partial dishwasher loads can use less water than washing by hand.

segments.title: Hot water heater energy cost
segments.summary: The hosts explain that handwashing draws continuously heated tap water, while a dishwasher heats water only during its cycle. An Energy Star dishwasher run four times a week is estimated at about 130 dollars of energy per year.

segments.title: Loading habits and household dishwashing
segments.summary: Josh describes his Tetris-style loading and his wife's approach of running small loads. They discuss household dish counts and the difficulty of doing dishes once a week.

segments.title: Pre-rinsing and scraping dishes
segments.summary: The hosts discuss pre-rinsing, quoting Noah Horowitz of the Natural Resources Defense Council that pre-rinsing wastes water and energy. Modern dishwashers can clean food that is only scraped, unlike older models.

segments.title: Upgrading machines and handwashing without a dishwasher
segments.summary: The hosts advise upgrading very old dishwashers if affordable, note that even older machines can beat handwashing, and describe filling a two-tub sink with soapy water and rinse water instead of running the tap.

segments.title: Closing banter and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts joke about wasteful habits such as running water over melting ice, then thank listeners and sign off with the show credits.
